    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A latest deal with Miami-Dade County will help American Airlines solidify and eventually expand its maintenance operations at Miami International Airport.

    Sources indicate that the county announced this week that it will buy a hangar and maintenance space at Miami International from a third-party owner and lease it directly to American for its MRO operations. The acquisition includes Hangar 890, Building 891, 10.2 acres of land, and a 2.2-acre parking lot.

    According to the Miami Herald, American already leases the property and uses it for maintenance work, but a change in ownership from private jet operator Aero Miami to the county will give American more leeway to develop the space as it sees fit. The new lease with the county will run for 20 years and cost American $67.8 million, the newspaper said.

    According to recent reports, the airline aims to keep more than 650 aircraft maintenance workers at the facility. It has also agreed to complete about $13.9 million in building repairs.

    “Miami is a cornerstone of American’s international network and a consequential part of our long-term growth strategy,” American Senior Vice President of Miami Operations Juan Carlos Liscano said in a news release. “This agreement reinforces our dedication to our Miami team and preserves our ability to continue growing our network to more destinations around the world for our customers.”.

    American is the largest airline at Miami, carrying more than half of all passengers there.

    Sources indicate that san Francisco International Airport (SFO) is facing a significant coastal flooding threat during one of the busiest travel periods of the year, with officials warning that exceptionally high tides could overwhelm vulnerable sections of its airfield. The National Weather Service (NWS) is forecasting water levels approaching 9 feet (almost 3 meters) or potentially higher around San Francisco Bay between November 24 and 26, coinciding with the Thanksgiving travel rush.

    Unusually high king tides, storm surge, warmer ocean temperatures, and an approaching winter storm are raising concerns about the airport's ability to keep its airfield and surrounding infrastructure clear of seawater. Although SFO is preparing for potential flooding, the situation could create additional complications for passengers, airlines, and airport operations during the holiday period.

    According to the Los Angeles Times, both SFO and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK) are facing potential flooding as exceptionally high tides approach Northern California. NWS meteorologists warned of extreme coastal flooding along the San Francisco Bay shoreline, with water levels potentially exceeding 9 feet depending on the storm surge. The forecast is concerning because SFO's seawalls are not uniformly high, leaving certain sections more vulnerable to overtopping.

    According to Deep Arrival, NWS also warned that water levels along SFO's shoreline could reach approximately 9.9 feet (3 meters) during the most concerning periods. The airport's seawall stretches for more than seven miles, but some vulnerable sections are reportedly only 8 feet high. The southeastern corner near Runway 28 Left is particularly exposed, while the northern ends of both runways also feature lower sections. It remains unclear whether the runways or taxiways themselves will experience flooding.

    The airport is already preparing for the possibility of seawater entering its airfield. According to Deep Arrival, SFO spokesperson Doug Yakel noted the airport was prepared to respond and maintain safe operations. Crews are clearing drainage areas, inspecting pump stations, and positioning sandbags and emergency flood barriers.

    According to recent reports, the flooding threat is being driven by several overlapping weather and astronomical factors. The NWS explains that unusually high king tides, thermal expansion from warmer ocean temperatures, and storm surge are combining to push Bay water levels toward historic territory. According to its November 22 forecast discussion, major to extreme coastal flooding is expected, with an impactful storm forecast to affect the region on Tuesday and Wednesday.

    According to recent reports, the NWS predicts the San Francisco tide gauge could reach 8.4 feet on Tuesday, November 24, and 8.6 feet (2.6 meters) on Wednesday, November 25, above mean lower low water. Thursday's predicted level is 8.2 feet (2.5 meters). These figures include the forecast tidal conditions, with additional storm-related water potentially worsening the situation. The previous record at San Francisco's Crissy Field gauge was 8.66 feet (2.63 meters), recorded in January 1983, according to the Los Angeles Times.

    The implications extend beyond airport infrastructure. Highway 101, an important access route for SFO passengers, could also experience flooding, potentially making it difficult for travelers and airport employees to reach the terminals. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has urged residents to avoid unnecessary journeys, particularly between Monday afternoon and Wednesday. The city is also suspending parking meter and time-limit enforcement during that period to help residents move their vehicles away from vulnerable areas, according to Deep Arrival.

    Industry observers note that the timing could hardly be worse for the airport, with Thanksgiving traditionally generating substantial domestic travel demand across the United States. Any flooding affecting SFO's runways, taxiways, or surrounding access roads could complicate an already busy operating environment. However, officials have not confirmed that flight cancellations or runway closures will be necessary, and the airport is continuing its preparations to maintain safe operations.

    OAK nearby is also monitoring the situation, although its infrastructure appears better positioned to withstand the predicted water levels. Deep Arrival reports that the airport has raised its perimeter dike to 13 feet (4 meters), reaching 17 feet (5 meters) in certain locations, and does not right now expect flooding. Meanwhile, the NWS anticipates drier conditions on Thanksgiving Day itself before another storm system potentially arrives during the following weekend.

    We recommend that our readers departing from SFO between November 24 and 26 monitor airline notifications and airport updates. The greatest concern is around late-morning high tides on Tuesday and Wednesday, when storm surge could push water beyond vulnerable seawall sections. Although flooding remains a forecast risk, not a confirmed operational disruption, the combination of high water levels and Thanksgiving passenger volumes presents a serious challenge for the airport and could disrupt travelers.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lufthansa is the “flagship” airline of Lufthansa Group, yet somehow, is the least profitable airline in the whole organization.
    • Sources indicate that unfortunately things haven’t turned out so great.
    • Well, Lufthansa pilots are just days from possibly being able to strike again, no agreement has been reached for long term peace with employees, and management is threatening to massively shrink its mainline operation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lufthansa is the “flagship” airline of Lufthansa Group, yet somehow, is the least profitable airline in the whole organization. 2026 was supposed to be an exciting turnaround year for Lufthansa, as it’s even the carrier’s 100th anniversary.

    Sources indicate that unfortunately things haven’t turned out so great. Earlier this year, the carrier dealt with massive labor complications, and back-to-back-to-back strikes. Just a few months ago, the company’s senior management claimed it wanted to turn over a latest leaf with labor relations, and stop fighting with employees, so that it could find long term solutions.

    How is that working out? Well, Lufthansa pilots are just days from possibly being able to strike again, no agreement has been reached for long term peace with employees, and management is threatening to massively shrink its mainline operation. In other words, it’s just another day at Lufthansa!

    In a recent development, lufthansa and its pilots have been in negotiations for quite some time over the future of the company. As you’d expect, broadly speaking, negotiations revolve around pay and future flying opportunities. As you’d expect at any airline, employees want as much flying as possible, and as big of a fleet as possible, since that’s what maximizes their compensation.

    The glitch with Lufthansa Group management is that the organization’s solution to everything is to simply create new, low cost subsidiaries. And if Lufthansa Group management doesn’t like the terms with its subsidiaries, then it just shuts down the subsidiaries and creates new ones.

    In a recent development, so that brings us to the current concern. Essentially, Lufthansa’s problem is that the airline doesn’t make money on short haul flights, given high costs and intense competition. So we’ve seen the carrier increasingly outsourcing this flying to Lufthansa City Airlines, a subsidiary with lower operating costs, operating the same kinds of planes as you’ll see in the mainline fleet.

    In a recent development, lufthansa is asking its pilots to accept wage freezes, and is promising a certain level of career development opportunities. Pilots aren’t happy with what’s being proposed, so what’s Lufthansa’s solution?

    Management is reportedly proposing a new strategy to the supervisory board, which would see the core Lufthansa brand massively reduce its regional flying, and largely outsource this to lower cost operations, like Lufthansa City Airlines. The idea would be to make Lufthansa primarily a long haul airline, and then have much of the short haul flying be operated by a subsidiary.

    Lufthansa’s mainline fleet presently consists of 260+ planes, with another 120+ planes on order. One proposal would see the mainline fleet reduced to 100 long haul aircraft and 100 short haul aircraft, with other planes being assigned to Lufthansa City Airlines.

    One radical proposal could even see Lufthansa exclusively have a long haul fleet and ditch short haul flying, though it’s noted that this isn’t the most likely scenario, and it could take several years for something like that to be implemented.

    Keep in mind that going back to 2017, Lufthansa had guaranteed pilots a minimum fleet size of 325 aircraft, but it terminated that agreement at the end of 2021. So it’s really hard for employees to trust any promises by management, when they can just be terminated.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s no denying that labor relations can be incredibly challenging, and that the economics of intra-Europe flying are also tough, when you have competitors like Ryanair, though Lufthansa doesn’t face nearly as much competition on that front as other carriers. Then again, Frankfurt (FRA) and Munich (MUC) aren’t exactly massively leisure destinations either.

    Most airline employees want their company to succeed, and just want to be compensated fairly. Admittedly economics don’t always align. But what I find incredibly toxic is the approach taken by Lufthansa management. Let’s compare it to a marriage (which I think is a fair way to view the relationship between management and employees, since they’re “stuck” with one another).

    Lufthansa’s approach is to constantly threaten employees by saying that “if you don’t do what we want, we’ll just get rid of you.” That’s simply not a good faith way to approach things. Why would Lufthansa employees trust management, when they’ve repeatedly torn up contracts, and shown employees they simply don’t care? It would be like threatening to leave your spouse every time you have an concern, rather than trying to find a solution.

    Sources indicate that nothing against Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr personally, but I don’t understand how the board thinks he’s the best person for the job. Where’s the accountability for the endless management mistakes that have horribly impacted Lufthansa’s bottom line? Lufthansa’s employees are paying the price for the lack of success that comes as a result of all of Lufthansa’s errors, from the botched Allegris rollout, to Lufthansa’s very bad luck with new aircraft orders.

    Recent findings suggest that and before anyone says “oh, but the unions,” contrast what has happened at Lufthansa Group to what has happened at Air France-KLM, under the leadership of Ben Smith. Smith has now been CEO at Air France for over eight years, and there hasn’t been a single strike under his leadership. Under the previous Air France-KLM CEO, there were endless strikes, and the situation got so bad that senior executives were being chased up a fence and having their clothes ripped off.

    It has been revealed that this highlights that good labor relations absolutely can happen, balancing the needs of employees and the company. But it requires showing employees that you actually care about the company and their future. What was one of Smith’s first orders of business when he took the job at Air France-KLM? He eliminated Joon, the low cost carrier at the airline that was supposed to basically be a labor arbitrage opportunity. That was a way to show employees how much he respected them, and that he wanted a fair agreement, rather than one that would undermine them.

    Meanwhile Spohr’s solution to literally everything is to just threaten to start newly introduced subsidiaries or shut down existing subsidiaries. The irony is that Spohr started his career as a pilot, so you’d think he’d have respect for employees, having been on the other side. But clearly once he became senior management, his love for aviation turned into disdain for employees.

    In a recent development, A few months ago, Lufthansa management claimed it wanted to turn over a newly introduced leaf when it comes to labor relations. That didn’t last long, because now the airline is back to its “do what we say or we’ll create a new subsidiary” approach.

    Recent findings suggest that I don’t have a strong opinion on the exact negotiations as such. Obviously it’s a tough time for aviation, and intra-Europe flying is challenging. But if you ask me, the toxicity that has been created by Lufthansa management due to the lack of good faith negotiations just can’t be undone.

    If your only solution to everything is “oh, we’ll create a upcoming subsidiary,” and if that doesn’t work, maybe it’s time for a new strategy. The fact that American CEO Robert Isom and Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr still have their jobs are two of the industry’s greatest mysteries.

    What do you make of Lufthansa’s latest threat to employees?

    Progressive advocates call on House Democrats to force Cuba vote

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May.
    • Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the problem is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.
    • According to recent reports, “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the problem is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.

    According to recent reports, “The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday. “In the midterm elections, U.S. voters resoundingly rejected a foreign policy of war and domination, and made clear their desire for Congress to act forcefully to rein in the Trump administration.

    Holding a vote would demonstrate that Democrats recognize the urgency facing the Cuban people, and would help set the tone for an assertive agenda of peace, diplomacy and respect for international law in the 120th Congress, the letter added.

    In a recent development, at issue is a war powers resolution introduced in May by Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., and House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., that would call on the president “to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Cuba, unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force.”.

    Industry observers note that the letter was sent to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of Newly introduced York, Meeks and House Rules Committee ranking member Jim McGovern, D-Mass. It was signed by prominent anti-war groups such as Win Without War, Just Foreign Policy, the Friends Committee on National Legislation, Indivisible and Code Pink.

    Advocates are frustrated that House Democrats have not forced a vote on a Cuba war powers resolution even as they have forced multiple war powers votes on Iran and see it as an example of leadership that is at odds with the progressive wing of the party. One advocate who requested anonymity to speak candidly stated it’s their understanding Democratic leaders are hesitant to make potentially vulnerable Florida members of the caucus vote on the problem.

    Spokespeople for Jeffries and Meeks did not respond to requests for comment Wednesday on whether Democrats will force a vote before the end of the year, what their reasoning is if they don’t and whether they plan to bring up a vote next year.

    It has been revealed that senate Democrats sought to force a vote on a similar resolution earlier this year, but Republicans in that chamber successfully derailed the effort. Senate Republicans raised a point of order that the resolution was not entitled to privileged status under the War Powers Resolution since U.S. troops aren't actively engaged in combat against Cuba. The point of order was sustained in a mostly party-line vote of 51-47.

    Senate Democrats later introduced another Cuba war powers resolution, which they have not tried to force a vote on and have not signaled they will do so before the end of the year.

    The resolutions have come amid several veiled threats from President Donald Trump suggesting eventual military action against Cuba.

    “I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt last week when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba.

    “Frankly, I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump said, adding he would “certainly consider” taking military action.

    Trump’s comments are on top of a pressure campaign his administration has been waging against Cuba. Since January, the United States has imposed a blockade of oil shipments to the island, causing fuel shortages that have led to lengthy blackouts and aggravated an economic crisis.

    While the Senate vote in April did not go Democrats’ way, advocates still saw it as sending a strong message.

    In a recent development, “Despite falling short of the majority, this was among the strongest votes in congressional history against the use of blockades, and one of the most notable stands Congress has taken against U.S. economic sanctions toward Cuba in over six decades,” the letter from progressive organizations said. “The House should take a similarly forceful action at this crucial moment.”.

    According to recent reports, the House vote, even if successful, would be largely symbolic since the measure Democrats can force a vote on is a concurrent resolution. Concurrent resolutions are widely considered to be nonbinding even if cleared by both chambers of Congress since they do not get a presidential signature, though anti-war advocates dispute that applies to war powers.

    The progressive groups in their letter called for “decisive leadership” in forcing a vote on the matter.

    “Across the political spectrum,” the letter stated, “Americans do not want another regime change war, nor an open-ended, nation-building project abroad based on false pretenses — especially not when escalation risks exposing the United States to upcoming national security risks, placing US servicemembers in harm’s way, stoking regional instability, and becoming the latest chapter in a long history of harmful U.S. regional policies that have fueled mass migration to U.S. shores.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

    Sources indicate that people are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

    An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉.

    Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:.

    What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

    I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

    Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a upcoming chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

    Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”.

    ChatGPT reveals you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

    Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”.

    Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”.

    ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

    You can watch the video for yourself below.

    A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt).

    According to recent reports, I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

    Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:.

    It has been revealed that okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:.

    In a recent development, to me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

    If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

    By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

    According to recent reports, while the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

    #122663. How Much Narrower Economy Seats Get When Airlines Fly 10-Abreast Cabins

    How Much Narrower Economy Seats Get When Airlines Fly 10-Abreast Cabins

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the discussion of how narrow economy-class seats are when fitted 10-abreast vs.
    • According to recent reports, the A330 (including A330neo) and Boeing 787 airliners are typically nine-abreast aircraft, although some earlier mainline Boeing 787s were configured eight-abreast in economy.
    • Both the Boeing 777 and the Airbus A350 were originally designed for nine-abreast seating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the discussion of how narrow economy-class seats are when fitted 10-abreast vs. nine-abreast is largely restricted to the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350. These two aircraft cabins are sized so that they are variously configured nine-abreast or 10-abreast. The massive A380 was wide enough so that it was only fitted with 10-abreast economy seating. Nine-abreast was unnecessary for the Superjumbo, even for premium-heavy mainline carriers, while regulations preclude any consideration of 11-abreast configuration.

    According to recent reports, the A330 (including A330neo) and Boeing 787 airliners are typically nine-abreast aircraft, although some earlier mainline Boeing 787s were configured eight-abreast in economy. Today, Japan Airlines remains the only airline to configure its flagship Dreamliners eight-abreast. The A330 and 787 are not realistically wide enough for a 10-abreast configuration.

    Both the Boeing 777 and the Airbus A350 were originally designed for nine-abreast seating. The Boeing 777 was developed as a luxury long-haul aircraft that would offer relatively generous seat width with a 3-3-3 layout. This made it one of the more comfortable high-capacity widebodies. The original 777s came with an internal cabin width of around 19 feet, 3 inches (5.87 meters). They were all configured nine-abreast.

    Later, Boeing 777-200LRs and -300ERs widened this to 19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters). The A350 followed almost two decades after the 777 originally entered service and followed a similar philosophy. But while it was called the 'Xtra Wide Body' (XWB), Airbus trimmed its width relative to the Triple Seven. Its width was considered spacious enough for a comfortable nine-seat economy configuration.

    These Airbus A350s were built with an internal cabin width of 18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters). The old-production standard A350s were wider than the early Boeing 777s, but they also came at a later time when pressures for denser seating had increased. All these aircraft were physically and legally capable of fitting ten abreast (3-4-3), but airlines chose not to.

    Recent findings suggest that as a rule of thumb, low-cost airlines concentrate on regional travel with the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 families. Long-haul international routes have been the domain of mainline carriers. Low-cost carriers work in a market segment that pushes for denser seating to reduce the cost per seat. Meanwhile, mainline carriers put more emphasis on premium seating and their premium brands. However, some low-cost carriers have moved into the long-haul leisure route market segment.

    Sources indicate that the two sister low-cost, long-haul, leisure airlines, Air Caraïbes and French Bee, have both purchased fleets of A350s. These are original production A350s, and both use the 3-4-3 (10-abreast) economy seating layout. This allows Frenchbee to achieve the A350-1000's maximum certified seat count of 480 (40 premium and 440 economy). Air Caraïbes also has the same configuration on some of its A350-1000s.

    19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters).

    19 feet, 3 inches (5.86 meters).

    19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters).

    Not standardized (approx. 18+ inches).

    19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters).

    18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters).

    18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters).

    18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters).

    18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters).

    The result is rather squishy. The published seat width for these economy seats is around 16 inches (41 cm). For reference, the industry average across the airline industry for economy class seats is 17 to 18 inches (about 43–46 cm). These two low-cost airlines are the only ones to have configured their old production A350s in this way. They can because their marketing is not so much concerned with onboard comfort; it's about getting passengers to far-flung leisure destinations as cheaply as possible. Just endure the flight.

    It has been revealed that historically, airlines configured their Boeing 777-200LRs and 777-300ERs nine-abreast (3-3-3), giving economy class passengers 18–18.5 inches (46–47 cm) in seat width. At the same time, market forces increasingly favored a high-density economy-class cabin. This generation of 777 was around four inches (nine cm) wider than the older aircraft.

    Today, most of the world's 777-300ERs have been fitted or retrofitted to seat 10-abreast, cutting the seat width to approximately 17 inches (43 cm). Some carriers have resisted the trend, notably Japan Airlines, ANA, Korean Air, and Singapore Airlines. But most, including premium-branded airlines like Qatar and Emirates, are now 10-abreast.

    Sources indicate that but even with the nine-abreast hold-outs, it has sometimes not been for the want of trying. In September 2025, Korea's JoongAng reported, "Korean Air is reconsidering its strategy to change the seating layout in economy class from a “3-3-3” to a tighter “3-4-3” arrangement after a mounting backlash from consumers." Korean Air has not yet published a final seat map or official cabin configuration for its ordered Boeing 777-9 aircraft, but it would be surprising if it retains the nine-abreast configuration.

    In a recent development, at 19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters), the 777-300ER was already wide enough for most mainline carriers to configure economy class 10-abreast. The incoming Boeing 777-9 and 777-8 (777X) come with thinner walls, allowing them to have a cabin width of 19 feet, 7 inches (5.97 meters). Boeing actively trolls Airbus and its A350, saying on its 777X product page, "Up to 40 cm (16 inches) wider than the A350.".

    In a recent development, the extra width will give the remaining holdout airlines more freedom to opt for the denser layout. ​​​​​In November 2026, Singapore Airlines revealed its latest 777-9 cabin with 17.6 inches (44.7 cm) for economy seats in a 3-4-3 configuration. The 777-9's cabin is wider and longer than the 777-300ER, but this will not necessarily increase the aircraft's density, as the vast majority of 777-300ERs are already 10-abreast. Ironically, the opposite is almost true because other market forces are pushing for more premium seating.

    The Boeing 777-300ER is certified to carry up to 550 passengers in an ultra-high density layout. The 777-9 has more cabin space to fit even more seats, but Boeing is limiting its maximum exit-limit seat count by 75 seats (to 475) or by 110 seats (to 440), depending on the door configuration. Put another way, the 777-9 is envisioned to have more business and premium economy seats, while the already standard 10-abreast economy will benefit from a few more inches of lateral space. The economy class cabin is expected to shrink.

    Recent findings suggest that as stated, the old production A350s have an internal cabin width of approximately 18 feet, 5 inches (5.60 meters). Without introducing a fresh variant or generation, Airbus introduced a new production standard that increases the usable cabin length and thins the aircraft walls. This allows the new-production standard cabin width to be 18 feet, 9 inches (5.72 meters). The first new-production standard A350s were delivered in 2022.

    Recent findings suggest that for airlines retaining the nine-abreast seating, it allows the typical economy seat width to grow from approximately 18 inches (46 cm) up to 18.7 inches (47.5 cm). That will be welcome to passengers. However, it also made 10-abreast seating more feasible. These latest aircraft with 10-abreast seating can accommodate 17-inch (43 cm) seats, bringing it closer to the conventional industry standard for economy seating.

    Sources indicate that to date, Philippine Airlines appears to be the only mainline carrier to opt for 10-abreast economy on upcoming production standard A350s. It is able to offer up to an inch more in seat width than French bee, but also has to trim more than an inch relative to airlines operating the A350 in nine-abreast. With the airline industry being a game measured in a couple of marginal inches and pressure for dense economy seating, it's possible more carriers will follow suit.

    According to recent reports, the Boeing 777 was originally designed as a nine-abreast airliner, but it has since grown by eight inches (17 cm) in cabin width over its life. This has allowed it to transition to a 10-abreast airliner without having to sacrifice much of its original spaciousness. The original economy class seats were around 18–18.5 inches (46–47 cm), and the next generation is expected to be around 18 inches (46 cm). This may not be an improvement for economy class passengers, but it is not catastrophic either.

    The A350 echoes the 777's path, while also being much more constrained. The A350 can be and is configured 10-abreast, but this reduces the seat width to 16–17 inches (41-43 cm). But there is also some degree of an apples-to-oranges comparison here. For economy passengers, the 777-9 doesn't normally have the advantage. They will be configured 10-abreast, while the A350 is almost always nine-abreast.

    Recent findings suggest that the upcoming-production-standard nine-abreast A350 has a meaningful advantage of approximately 1.1 inches (2.8 cm), or 6.25% more seat width per economy passenger compared with a 10-abreast 777-9. This A350's nine-abreast vs. the 777X's 10-abreast comparison is important as it's a better representation of the actual industry standard. It's also worth noting that the A350 is more versatile than the 777X in terms of its missions and airlines. Only a relatively limited number of mainline carriers are purchasing the 777X, while a larger range of airlines, including low-cost airlines, are purchasing (often smaller) A350 fleets.

    • Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S.

    The British first edition of The Managerial Revolution that I picked up in a Charing Cross Road shop a quarter century ago tells us much about the work itself. I’ve read it four times, conscripted it as an airplane companion, and brought it to the beach. Yet its binding remains strong, its cover quite flexible, and its pages yellowing but intact. We no longer much refer to let alone read such 1941 bestsellers as Clifton Fadiman’s Reading I’ve Liked or Margaret Leech’s Reveille in Washington. But James Burnham, much like my strong and solid copy of his most famous book, endures.

    Recent findings suggest that burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation. The Managerial Revolution, anticipating as it did the ascension of technocrats, specialists, and the bureaucratic elite as a sort of ruling class, surely helped in that regard. Burnham remains read, despite no Burnhamite clique in academia or organized faction among movement conservatives dedicated to advancing his ideas. Kirkians, Straussians, and Randians exist. Why no James Burnham Preservation Society with an accompanying secret handshake?

    Daniel J. Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S. Meyer, is an American Spectator senior editor, visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution, and YouTuber @RightWingWilderness.

    On “The Complex Reputation of James Burnham”.

    Industry News: Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday showed how poisonous the politics could become.
    • Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday showed how poisonous the politics could become.

    Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    In a recent development, “I think it’s outrageous,” said Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking key.”.

    Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    Industry observers note that "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he remarked on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson remarked Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    Johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

    Recent findings suggest that there is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson said Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    It has been revealed that sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability glitch, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” mentioned Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    • Industry observers note that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”).

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

    It has been revealed that in the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

    This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

    This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”.

    According to recent reports, ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes.

    Video taken from the jet bridge highlights masked ICE agents trying to arrest people on the jet bridge.

    Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines remarked ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv.

    As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

    Here’s how ICE explained its actions:.

    In a recent development, on November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

    In a recent development, during the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

    According to recent reports, the individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

    Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

    On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws. During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5.

    The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:.

    We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

    Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:.

    ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

    Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:.

    In a recent development, we are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible.

    There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”.

    Sources indicate that Q: You think your deportation policy went too far?Trump: I think it might be too tough. pic.twitter.com/NKhFjZKxnd.

    Sources indicate that no matter how you feel about deportations as such, having them go down in this way for someone who simply overstayed their visa is a step too far, in my opinion. I mean, it’s one thing if we’re talking about a violent criminal on some sort of watch list, but that’s clearly not the case here.

    Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

    Industry observers note that and here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look. It reminds me of another incident we recently saw at Las Vegas Airport (LAS). Like, is this person being robbed in the terminal, or is this an official law enforcement operation?

    On Saturday, an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by a few hours after ICE agents stormed a jet bridge to arrest someone, leading to a larger fight, which also caused more arrests. It’s one thing if such a disruptive operation were targeting a violent criminal, but is this really the way that someone who overstays a visa should be apprehended?

    #122655. The American Genius of Madden

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (863 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    The American Genius of Madden

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, hang on at the start of David O.
    • The key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football.
    • Madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, hang on at the start of David O. Russell’s Madden, as its story of the Oakland Raiders football coach John Madden shifts between semidocumentary and biopic. Russell’s uneven, sketchy narrative steadily turns into a probing human comedy. It’s also a slyly monumental tale of American genius found in an Everyman’s commonplace ambition.

    The key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football. Cage enters the mindset of a sports fanatic who is also an artist, devising plays and strategies that, considering his size and vision, earn him the nickname “Buddha.” But this is not one of those freak-outs that Cage is known for; he seems to transform himself into John Candy — broad-beamed with a tuft of blond hair and a convincing smile. Cage commits to this genial eccentric who, despite his unreachable idiosyncrasy, is harmless, lovable yet tough — an authentic, original American.

    Madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend. This thick-and-thin Laurel-and-Hardy pair sustain an unlikely partnership. It’s one of the most remarkable depictions of brotherhood in movies — a friendship that persists over temperamental tensions, even after Madden leaves the team and pursues media entrepreneurship to sustain his love of the sport. Madden the broadcaster converts his playbook ingenuity and follows his father’s advice: “Get away with doing what you love for as long as you possibly can.”.

    Sources indicate that russell redeems himself with the oddest-yet-normal collection of American eccentrics. Acting on the edge of parody, Cage and Bale, with their uncanny sincerity, reward Russell’s interest in quirkiness. (Madden hears Davis’s voice in his head.) The fascinating scoundrels of Russell’s terrific American Hustle were preoccupied with manipulating one another. Here, friendship, comradeship, teamwork, and family complications are genuinely recognizable. Scenes that emulate a documentary approach — Madden’s wife Virginia (gung ho comedienne Kathryn Hahn) rivals Jennifer Lawrence’s volatility when speaking directly to the camera — satirize realism to fulfill the non-cynical view of national character that Russell fumbled in the bohemian sojourn of Amsterdam. No wonder De Niro is left out of this particular silver-lined playbook.

    Nicolas Cage (John Madden) in Madden.

    Chuck Zlotnick/Amazon MGM Studios.

    The patchwork of styles in Madden suggests that Russell investigates American eccentricity as he goes along, finding his way back to the coast-to-coast realness that made his Flirting with Disaster so exhilarating (as in Madden’s surreal, unapologetic pitch for the unique holiday dish the Turducken). Russell adopts Madden’s football-analysis style, such as on-screen telestrator vectors, to humorously examine Madden’s own career shifts and twists of personality (Madden instructing his players, or meeting colleagues Pat Summerall, Howard Cosell, and Bob Costas).

    Sources indicate that A dull-witted filmmaker, say James Cameron, would choose an “immersive” style for a movie concerned with the gestalt of football. But Russell’s film is also about the phenomenon of a sport that becomes a vanguard of technology and culture. Madden is pursued by Trip Hawkins (John Mulaney), founder of video game firm EA (Electronic Arts), who wants to translate Madden’s football theories for a upcoming generation of at-home fans and gamers. Hawkins’s proposal is scored to Beethoven’s Ninth — another example of Russell’s wit, matching the film’s eclectic score from Barry White and Talking Heads to N.W.A. (“You don’t want to know what that means,” Davis says to Madden.).

    Through Madden and Hawkins’s acumen, Russell treats the discovery of a latest world as an aftereffect of folk intelligence and ingenuity. Genius is kidded when Hawkins’s team of four-eyed computer nerds demonstrate jock potential after applying Madden’s plays to their algorithms. It’s a sweet way of conveying the phenomenon that would turn EA’s Madden NFL video game franchise into a $4 billion enterprise (some estimates raise that into double digits), with annual compensation going to the Madden family estate.

    More notable, Russell (who co-wrote the script with Cambron Clark) sees Madden as a visionary who proudly summarizes TV sportscasting as “They state the obvious, which is f***ing boring.” My only complaint is that Robert Richardson’s photography tends toward frowzy (perhaps deliberately aping TV docs), not as splendid as Oliver Stone’s Any Given Sunday — the greatest football movie ever made.

    Madden itself shares biopic sensibility with John Ford’s The Wings of Eagles, respectfully eschewing its subject’s mortality for an optimistic appreciation of a man’s potential. It is unique to American character and the experience of competition and dreams of the NFL Hall of Fame that Madden shared with Al Davis. Russell’s tribute comes complete with a motto: “You make people feel good and alive and good to be American, and I’m not standing in the way of that.” Thus Russell proves his own resilience and the achievement of a new folkloric genre struggling to emerge.

    Armond White is National Review’s culture critic and the author of Fresh Position: The Prince Chronicles and Make Spielberg Great Again: The Steven Spielberg Chronicles.

    On “The American Genius of Madden”.

    In a recent development, rakuten is my favorite online shopping portal, and if you’re not using it, you’re leaving rewards on the table. Through December 31, 2026, if you join Rakuten through a qualifying referral link and spend $50 within the first 90 days, you’ll receive a $50 bonus. The person referring you can also receive $50. This is even an opportunity to earn Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Points at a very favorable ratio.

    Taking advantage of this Rakuten sign-up bonus is truly a no-brainer, as I’d view this as a way to get $50 worth of stuff for (basically) free. For that matter, you’re missing out more broadly if you’re not earning additional rewards for your online shopping, beyond what you earn with your credit card.

    In this post I’d like to go over all the details of Rakuten, including how the Rakuten referral bonus works, and the easiest way to maximize it (as it’s really easy to take advantage of, even if you don’t think you have an immediate purchase in mind).

    Link: Sign-up for a Rakuten account with a best-ever $50 bonus.

    In a recent development, rakuten is a free online shopping and rewards platform that pays owners either cash back or points for the shopping they do online. Rakuten partners with over 3,500 online retailers, many of which are well known, ranging from Lowe’s, to Nike, to Target. The Rakuten shopping portal concept is simple — if you click through from Rakuten to the partner website, Rakuten tracks the purchase and gets paid a commission, and then you get a reward as well.

    According to recent reports, note that as a consumer, Rakuten is free to use. The commission is paid by the business, so you’ll pay the same price you’d pay if you just went directly to the retailer’s website. To maximize your savings, you can even download the Rakuten browser extension, which will automatically notify you when you can earn extra rewards.

    Sources indicate that I should mention that there are several online shopping portals out there to choose from, so Rakuten isn’t the only one. Personally I find that Rakuten is my favorite because it has among the largest selection of partners, it gives you the flexibility to earn cash back or points, and I also find the earnings rates to be very competitive.

    Sources indicate that it can always pay to use a site like Cashback Monitor to compare the earnings rates for retailers across portals, so that you’re maximizing your rewards. In some situations you may be better off using other portals, so it’s always worth understanding what your options are.

    Through December 31, 2026, Rakuten is offering a generous elevated refer-a-friend bonus. Specifically, if you refer a friend to Rakuten and they spend $50 within the first 90 days, then both the person referring and the person being referred each receive $50.

    This is truly a best-ever bonus, as we’ve previously only seen a bonus of up to $40 — though admittedly this offer has stuck around for quite some time.

    This is a very good deal. Essentially Rakuten is giving out $100 total for a $50 purchase, between the person referring and the person being referred. Long term you can potentially get even more value with Rakuten, as rewards can be converted into Amex or Bilt Points.

    Actually earning the $50 Rakuten sign-up bonus is really straightforward:.

    What’s the timeline with which you’ll actually receive the rewards? With Rakuten you’re paid (either in cash or points) once quarterly, and there’s a cutoff for payments, per the below chart.

    Sources indicate that rakuten partners with literally thousands of retailers, and an eligible purchase worth at least $50 with any eligible retail partner would qualify. When you click over to the partner site, just make sure you keep an eye on any exclusions, since some types of purchases may not qualify for rewards.

    There are also often amazing opportunities to earn up to 100% back or 100x points with select retailers, which is a rate at which I’d gladly buy points all day long, without even factoring in the service being sold. So I take advantage of these deals all the time, even if I don’t actually value the product.

    It has been revealed that if you’re not interested in that and don’t have anything you need to buy right now, there’s another creative option. There are easy ways to unlock the $50 bonus, including simply purchasing a $50 gift card through giftcards.com. This is so easy — you can pick up a $50 gift card with a variety of retailers, and then you’ll receive $50 in cash.

    To briefly explain that process, you’d enter giftcards.com in the search bar at the top of Rakuten’s website.

    According to recent reports, then click the “Shop Now” button, which will take you to giftcards.com. All your purchases while on that site will automatically be tracked.

    The website sells a variety of gift cards with popular retailers, including DoorDash, Uber, Delta, Southwest, Hulu, Netflix, Dominos, and many more.

    For example, you could buy a $50 DoorDash gift card at face value, and the code will be delivered by email within minutes.

    Once the purchase is complete, you should see Rakuten automatically tracking the purchase.

    Within an hour the purchase should be fully reflected — the Rakuten account will show a credit in the amount of the sign-up bonus, plus the rewards for the actual purchase (which will vary based on whether you choose to earn cash or points). As a standard, giftcards.com offers either 1% cash back, or one point per dollar spent, but sometimes we see increased offers (like right now).

    Taking advantage of this is the obvious choice, in my opinion:.

    The reason that Rakuten is my favorite shopping portal is because Rakuten rewards can be converted into Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points. The exact way this works depends on the currency you choose to earn.

    It has been revealed that with the Rakuten and Amex Membership Rewards partnership, you can consistently earn one point in lieu of one cent, assuming you have an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points. So if a retailer offers 10% cash back, you can instead earn 10x Amex points.

    In a recent development, based on my latest points valuations, Amex Membership Rewards points are worth 1.7 cents each, because of all the ways there are to redeem the points for first and business class international travel, while getting outsized value. To me that increases the value of the rewards by 70%.

    Industry observers note that this just requires changing one setting in your account, so it’s super easy. The only thing to be aware of is that this points earning opportunity doesn’t apply to the welcome bonus, but does apply to all spending beyond that.

    Recent findings suggest that that’s not the only opportunity, though. The Rakuten and Bilt Rewards partnership lets members earn Bilt Rewards points in lieu of cash back. Bilt elite members can earn one point in lieu of every one cent, while non-elite members can earn one point in lieu of every two cents. Much like Amex Membership Rewards points, I also value Bilt Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, as there are also many good uses of this points currency.

    What’s cool here is that your cash back can retroactively be converted into Bilt Points for the entire Rakuten “payout” period (roughly quarterly), and that means even the refer-a-friend bonus can be converted into points.

    If you have the choice between one Amex point or one Bilt point, I think many people might prefer the latter, given the value of the rewards, plus how hard they are to earn. However, if the ratio isn’t one point per cent, then I’d go with the Amex partnership instead.

    Beyond the rewards you earn directly with Rakuten, your spending with retailers can of course also earn credit card rewards.

    Industry observers note that rakuten’s co-branded Amex card is among the best cards for Rakuten spending, as it earns 4% cash back on those purchases, on up to $10,000 per calendar year. Beyond that, purchases with online retailers typically don’t qualify for any exciting bonus categories, so most consumers will want to use one of the best cards for everyday spending.

    #122648. Southwest Plans To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Says

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4193 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Southwest Plans To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Says

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4193 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines plans to stop making customers wait for batches of latest flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria.
    • I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar.
    • There’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines plans to stop making customers wait for batches of latest flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria. That would make it easier to lock in a family vacation or flights to a cruise—and give its international partners more opportunities to sell trips that include Southwest connections. I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar. They’re accepting reservations through September 29, 2027. Their next extension is planned for December 17, when they’ll open flights through November 6, 2027. That’s 324 days into the future. That December release is still a batch. The plan to replace these releases with a rolling window isn’t something I’ve seen anywhere other than from Enilria. Southwest Has Already Sold Flights More Than 300 Days Ahead There’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing. On April 26, 2024, Southwest announced its first booking window exceeding 300 days. It was selling travel through March 5, 2025—313 days ahead. At the time, Southwest said its historical range had been 180 to 250 days, citing vacation planning, meetings and groups, Hawaii, and its international destinations as reasons to sell further out. With batch releases, though, the window shrinks every day until the next extension. You might be able to book ten months ahead on release day, then considerably less several weeks later. A rolling calendar keeps adding dates. The reported change would give customers roughly the same planning horizon whenever they shop, without needing to track Southwest’s next release announcement. Shorter Schedules Meant Fewer Reservations To Fix I wrote about Southwest’s tradeoff back in 2020: waiting to publish let the airline offer a firmer schedule, but cost them customers who wanted to commit earlier. An airline can decide where to put its planes before selling the seats, or sell a provisional schedule and fix customers’ reservations when its plans change. Southwest preferred to finish more of that work first. That gave them room to adjust for seasonal demand and aircraft availability without disrupting as many purchased trips. Their technology made changing flights expensive. In a 2010 investor presentation, then-CEO Gary Kelly explained that when Southwest canceled a flight: we have to manually rebook every single customer on that flight Southwest completed its move to Amadeus Altéa in May 2017. This allowed for automated rebooking during disruptions, better connection planning, and more sophisticated inventory management. So the technology that makes a longer selling window practical has been there for years. The commercial case for using it has grown. International Partners Have A Reason To Want More Dates Southwest increasingly needs to appear wherever customers are shopping. I explained how the Expedia deal would change their incentives when it was announced in 2025. If a customer searches dates Southwest isn’t selling, competitors get the business before Southwest even enters the comparison. The airline had already expanded booking capabilities through agency reservation systems in 2020. More recently, SAP Concur shut down its old Southwest direct connection in July 2025 as Southwest’s new fare structure required a different booking path. And Southwest now lists 12 international airline partners, including Icelandair, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, and newly added French bee. These combined itineraries are sold through the partners’ websites and distribution channels. A foreign airline can have its flight available for sale while Southwest hasn’t opened the domestic connection yet. The partner can’t issue the complete itinerary using that Southwest flight. It may sell a connection on another U.S. airline instead and Southwest loses the passenger. That makes partner sales a strong reason to extend the window. The underlying partnership work also predates Elliott Management’s intervention. I covered Southwest recruiting to build airline partnerships in June 2022. And the longer schedule announcement came in April 2024. Even a roughly 330 day window won’t match every overseas partner. EVA Air sells flights up to 360 days ahead. This would narrow the gap, while still leaving some early international bookings out of Southwest’s reach. Earlier Booking Comes With More Time For Plans To Change Selling earlier gives Southwest more chances to win customers. Direct bookings bring cash in sooner. The recurring benefit comes from business Southwest otherwise would’ve lost, or from selling its existing seats more profitably. Against that are distribution costs, servicing reservations, and the work of repairing itineraries when schedules change. Customers should expect more exposure to schedule revisions when booking further ahead. A departure can move, a nonstop can become a connection, and a changed domestic flight can break the connection to an international departure. With assigned seating, moving passengers also means dealing with their seat selections. And the first day a flight goes on sale isn’t necessarily its cheapest day. Opening dates and opening inexpensive inventory are separate decisions. In fact, airlines may hold back cheap fares waiting to see how flights sell, and also figuring that eager buyers may be less price-sensitive. And there’s a real a problem buying Southwest’s cheapest cash tickets this far ahead. As I’ve covered before, Basic fare credits expire six months after the original purchase. Southwest says a voluntary cancellation after that deadline produces no flight credit. If you buy a Basic ticket 11 months ahead, then cancel two months before departure, you’ve already passed that deadline by three months. The original reservation is valid, but you get nothing if you cancel. I’d be much more comfortable using Rapid Rewards points for a speculative booking that far out. Cancel at least 10 minutes before the original departure and the points go back to the account, without the six month expiration attached to the cash fare.     On Personalized Pricing, the FTC Got Ahead of the Evidence

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (140 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that americans should expect their federal agencies to be staffed by experts who gather evidence meticulously before proposing regulations disinterestedly.
    • Last month, the FTC ordered nine major companies — Delta Air Lines, Uber, and Instacart among them — “to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices and compensation.” The agency, however, seems to have reached its conclusions already, given the contents of both its order and an enforcement policy proposed in August, which appears partial against personalized pricing and the businesses that employ it.
    • Vladlena Klymova is a policy analyst at the Taxpayers Protection Alliance.

    Sources indicate that americans should expect their federal agencies to be staffed by experts who gather evidence meticulously before proposing regulations disinterestedly. But that’s not what the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has done when it comes to personalized pricing.

    Last month, the FTC ordered nine major companies — Delta Air Lines, Uber, and Instacart among them — “to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices and compensation.” The agency, however, seems to have reached its conclusions already, given the contents of both its order and an enforcement policy proposed in August, which appears partial against personalized pricing and the businesses that employ it.

    Vladlena Klymova is a policy analyst at the Taxpayers Protection Alliance.

    On “On Personalized Pricing, the FTC Got Ahead of the Evidence”.

    How to avoid petty theft while traveling

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (129 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • Petty theft is a risk in many popular travel destinations, especially crowded tourist spots and public transportation hubs.
  • Travelers can reduce their vulnerability by minimizing valuables, blending in with locals and staying alert in busy areas.
  • Using theft-resistant bags, securing belongings and splitting up valuables are effective strategies to deter thieves.
  • Travel insurance may offer theft protection, but coverage varies, so reviewing your policy details is important.
  • Thieves often work in teams, creating distractions to target distracted travelers.
  • Public transportation and tourist attractions are common hotspots for pickpocketing incidents.
  • Scams can take many forms, from unsolicited help to aggressive sales tactics, so maintaining awareness is crucial.
